field.label: Enable monitor
field.help: Start the background monitor. It polls the enabled sources at the interval below and keeps a history of devices and events. Polling only reads; changes are made only from the Configuration page and only when "Allow changes" is ticked.

field.label: Allow changes
field.help: Let the plugin change the configuration of the switches (Switch page: port and PoE controls; Configuration page: every section). Off by default: the plugin then only reads. Sections that control access to the switch (management address and VLAN, accounts and passwords, login authentication, web service, certificates, firmware, access lists) and the port that leads to the firewall are never changed, so a mistake cannot lock the firewall out. The switch account needs administrator rights. Every change is recorded in Events and in the log.

field.label: Polling interval (seconds)
field.help: How often the devices are read. 60 seconds is a good default. Shorter intervals give smoother throughput figures but put more load on the switch web server; one poll of a 52-port switch takes about 5 seconds, and the switches are read one after the other.

field.label: Keep history (days)
field.help: Devices that were not seen for longer than this are forgotten, and older events are deleted.

field.label: Link flap warning
field.help: Warn about a port when the switch log holds at least this many link-down messages for it. Moments when many ports drop together (switch restart, firmware update) are ignored.

field.label: PoE budget warning (%)
field.help: Warn when the power drawn by PoE devices exceeds this share of the switch power budget.

field.label: Read the access points
field.help: Read the diagnostic page each Instant On access point publishes on the local network (model, serial, firmware, coordinator, cloud and time-sync status, reason of the last restart). This page needs no password. The list of wireless clients with SSID and signal is not available locally: it needs a cloud account.

field.label: Discover through the switch
field.help: Find access points through the LLDP neighbours of every switch. Each one is shown with its switch and port, link speed and PoE draw. Access points meshed over Wi-Fi are not plugged into a switch: add them below, or add a cloud account to see them.

field.label: Additional access points
field.help: IP addresses of access points that are not discovered automatically (meshed, or connected to a switch that is not monitored), separated by commas.

field.label: Diagnostic port
field.help: TCP port of the access point diagnostic page. Instant On uses 8080.
